title: The Field Brief
blurb: Daily scout surface for CR-Harness and adjacent agent-control research. Public sources only. Not an hourly Cao-style feed — refresh ~daily. Lives under CR-Harness (not hub homepage).

entries.title: SAG: invoke the critic only when admissible-action entropy / top-2 margin say it's worth it
entries.summary: Park, Im, Kwon et al., arXiv:2610.07335 (submitted 5 Oct 2026). Frames critique invocation as a step-wise decision: a training-free gate estimates critique utility from action-level ambiguity signals (global entropy and local top-2 margin over admissible actions), approximating the value of information; online bootstrapped self-improvement lets the actor internalize critic-assisted behaviour. Across three long-horizon interactive benchmarks and multiple backbones it improves the performance–cost trade-off vs no-critique and always-on critique. On ALFWorld, task success rises from 24.6% to 78.4% at a token budget comparable to ReAct (3.1x normalized token efficiency); a 7B actor with a 3B critic matches a 14B actor without critique.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: A concrete gate signal for CR: entropy and top-2 margin computed over the legal_actions distribution decide when to call a stronger model or reviewer. It's the same shape as the Jev confidence floor, now with published cost/benefit numbers.

entries.title: SharedKV-BT: node-local typed decisions with stage gating in behaviour trees
entries.summary: Wake, Wagle et al., arXiv:2610.07327 (submitted 5 Oct 2026). Each active behaviour-tree node exposes stage-local fields and candidates; Shared-KV scores the candidates in parallel and hands the selected decision to a separate execution system. On robot manipulation, mobile navigation and computer-use tasks, typed decisions are 2.36–4.15x faster than prompt-matched autoregressive decoding. On manipulation, joint decision accuracy goes from 75% to 94% and closed-loop success from 0% to 60%. Fixed-score policy replay showed stage gating prevented out-of-order actions and external postconditions prevented premature completion.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Stage-local candidate lists are legal_actions masking scoped by game phase (e.g. pick card → pick tile → confirm). Splitting a CR decision into staged typed fields, with execution and postconditions checked outside the model, is a testable alternative to one flat action list.

entries.title: Judged Useless, Queried Anyway: only a harness-enforced rule makes agents stop on their own evidence
entries.summary: Zhang, Wan, Yu et al., arXiv:2610.06191 (submitted 5 Oct 2026; first noted in the 10-06 brief). In a retrieval environment with controlled source failures, the seven agents tested call a failing source's results useless 97–100% of the time (where judgments are recorded), yet most rarely stop on that judgment. Prompt cues change when they stop, not what they stop on; a stopping rule or call cost in the prompt is followed at most partly. Stopping follows the evidence only when the harness enforces an integration step (answer after five consecutive results judged useless). That raises failing-source success for every model and keeps the stopping point fixed when the budget doubles. A preregistered replication on 300 fresh questions confirms the result.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Supports putting control rules in the harness rather than the prompt: if a CR agent keeps choosing actions it has itself labelled bad or rejected, a harness rule (e.g. after N rejected or self-flagged actions, force wait or escalate) is more reliable than telling it to stop.

entries.title: Learn2Play Bench: text games with novel rules to test learning from interaction
entries.summary: Li, Qiu, Zheng et al., arXiv:2610.08215 (submitted 6 Oct 2026; project site live). Newly designed text-based games with novel or counterintuitive rules, reproducible feedback and automatic scoring; game instances vary to test transfer. Evaluates backbones, self-evolving methods and harnesses. Findings: retaining complete action/feedback records supports learning better than summarizing them into rules; top human players beat the agents' peak scores, exploring more varied strategies and repeating actions less; with the backbone fixed, changing the harness can improve performance while lowering estimated inference cost. Abstract gives no headline numbers.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Mini Royale's rules aren't in pretraining either, so it's a learn-from-play setting. The raw-history-beats-summarized-rules finding argues for keeping full (action → result) logs in agent memory, and 'repeats actions less' is a cheap diagnostic to log per match.

entries.title: XiangqiBench: finding the move is not winning the game
entries.summary: Chai, Peng, Xiong et al., arXiv:2610.02425 (submitted 1 Oct 2026). Executable Chinese-chess benchmark: from 119 tactical endgames with forced mates, an LLM agent must actually deliver checkmate against an engine defender, through a REPL that separates real moves, state queries and forward simulation. 8,568 multi-turn trajectories from 12 frontier LLMs under two observation protocols. Three gaps: Conversion (models play the stored reference first move in 26.1% of Sighted trials, but only 13.9% of those end in a win); Consistency (leading model 38.7% pass@3 but 5.9% pass^3); Simulation (32.3% of accepted simulation calls stop on an illegal move, and in 49.3% of comparable cases the real defender replies differently from the agent's simulated line).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Direct warning against scoring CR on per-decision 'good move' metrics alone: decision_point accuracy can look fine while closed-loop match outcomes do not follow. Adopt pass^k (win all k seeds) next to pass@k, separate real actions from state queries/simulation in the action interface, and log illegal actions inside any agent-side lookahead.

entries.title: Kaggle Game Arena tech report: retry/forfeit harness rules as eval design
entries.summary: Doerschuk-Tiberi et al. (Kaggle + Google DeepMind), arXiv:2609.31473 (submitted 25 Sep 2026). Chess, Poker and Werewolf environments with open harness (google-deepmind/game_arena). Chess: legality enforced by the environment; an invalid move gets a bare 'invalid, retry' with diagnostics intentionally hidden, 3 retries, 4th failure = loss; retries ('rethinks') tracked as a reliability metric, and the report finds illegal moves concentrate later in games for weaker models. Poker: one retry, then defaults to check/fold; 20,000 hands per pair, 900,000 hands total, BB/100 with block bootstrap. Werewolf: parse failures past a retry cap force a turn forfeit. Per-game metrics: Bradley–Terry Elo, BB/100, game-theoretic eval.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: The most public, large-scale statement of the design choices CR must make at every decision_point: show the legal list or not, how much feedback on an illegal action, how many retries, and what the fallback is (loss vs conservative default vs forfeit). CR should declare these as a versioned harness policy and log rethink counts by match phase.

entries.title: REFLEX: Jev typed-choice gate + strong-LLM fallback, measured
entries.summary: Wu & Lim (NTU), arXiv:2609.26532 (submitted 22 Sep 2026). REFLEX uses Jev (jev-1.13.0) as a typed decision layer returning (choice, confidence); execute when c≥τ and executable, else fall back to a strong LLM. Frozen 100-task REFLEX-Sim: 95% success vs 88% strong-only with 72.7% fewer strong-model calls at τ=0.5; 66–72% call reduction across Qwen3.8-Max / Kimi K3 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro fallbacks. Honest limits: on BFCL, choosing which function is 98.4% accurate but deciding whether to call any is 52.0%; on τ²-bench a cheap Flash self-escalation cascade stays competitive. Larger action sets (K 10→50) and near-valid competitors reduce accuracy.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: First public controlled evaluation of exactly the jev-gameplay-decision-router idea: typed choice over an allowed set + confidence floor + fallback. Gives CR a metric template (GMR, risk–coverage/AURC, strong calls per success, commit-vs-defer error split) and a warning that legal_actions size and near-valid alternatives degrade the gate.

entries.title: Action-class diagnostic: Acc ≤ GAR exposes act/ask/refuse miscalibration
entries.summary: Zhao et al., arXiv:2609.00949 (1 Sep 2026). Decomposes multi-turn tool-calling failures into action-class miscalibration vs execution failure over TOOL_CALL/ASK/REFUSE/CONFIRM, with an upper bound Acc ≤ Gold Action Recall. Bound violations reveal state graders that mask wrong action classes; context-only perturbations can move accuracy +11.5 vs −21.0 pp across families on the same scenario.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR decision_points also have action classes (play card / wait-noop / escalate). Logging a gold/expected class separately from the chosen action id lets ETL catch outcome graders that reward lucky wins from the wrong class of decision.

entries.title: Jev at decision_point: typed Choice/Noul gate over legal_actions
entries.summary: TypeSafe Jev (OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13) returns Choice/Noul/Score with probabilities — no prose. Already LIVE on the fleet harness at confidence_floor 0.55 for CoS routing. Scout ask: wire the same router into Mini Royale gameplay at decision_point (legal_actions whitelist + cockpit path), not hub routing only. Prior art: AutoHarness/PTCG legal masks, R2V residual-risk escalate, confidence-gate act/ask/abstain, HarnessBridge reject-with-feedback.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already emits decision_point + legal_actions; Jev can Choice among legal ids or Noul-gate escalate/noop when conf<floor, with ETL logging of conf/fallback — reusable eval surface for latency vs false-escalate.

entries.title: AutoHarness: synthesize code that blocks illegal moves
entries.summary: DeepMind (Lou et al.): Gemini-2.5-Flash iteratively synthesizes an is_legal_action / propose_action code harness via Thompson-sampling tree search over environment feedback. Claims 100% legal-action rate across 145 TextArena games; smaller Flash+harness beats larger Pro on many 1P/2P evals. Direct analogue to CR-Harness legal_actions at decision_point.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already whitelists legal_actions — AutoHarness shows how to auto-build or regression-test that verifier from env feedback, and how illegal-move rate dominates LLM game losses.

entries.title: PTCG-Bench: legal-action masking swings card-game ratings
entries.summary: Hua et al.: Pokémon TCG benchmark for LLM agents with modular harness ablations (structured obs, legal-action masking, history). Removing legal-action masking drops Glicko-2 by ~118 points and raises invalid-action rate to ~16%. Self-evolution across rounds stays unstable. Closest public TCG analogue to Mini Royale decision_points.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Quantifies how much of ‘LLM skill’ is really the mask + observation schema — exactly what CR’s legal_actions + ETL should report per model–harness pair.

entries.title: Adversarial Review: structured disagreement beats naive dual LGTM
entries.summary: Qiu & Gill (arXiv:2608.18167): reviewer + critic protocol; naive AR collapses into false consensus; three-way critic verdicts (AGREE / DISAGREE_EVIDENCE / DISAGREE_CONCERN) lift SWE-PRBench F1. Portable as SKILL.md. Maps onto fleet blind dual-LGTM (Astra + second seat).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Fleet coding loop already wants blind dual LGTM; AR’s typed disagreement is a concrete protocol upgrade for Github Bot EM / Manage review babysitting — also useful when reviewing CR cockpit/eval PRs.
